Article Title: 'Contamination' in fuel, says SIAM, later retracts
Article Text:
SIAM says corrosion of vehicle parts due to high chloride presence in fuel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Auto industry body SIAM flagged concerns over "high chloride" presence and moisture content in fuel resulting in a "huge increase" in issues related to vehicle parts and replacements, including fuel pumps, fuel injectors and EGR valve. It demanded stringent checks, arguing that contamination raises a wrong impression about E20 fuel in customers' minds, report Dipak Dash & Aabhas Sharma.Late evening, SIAM said it has since "withdrawn" the letter sent to petroleum ministry on July 28 that had raised these concerns, which were based on investigations of failure of vehicle parts.Some numbers quoted in the communication need authentication through collection of elaborate data from various regions across the country followed by a comprehensive consultation with our member OEMs. MoPNG has also instituted 3ppm guidelines for chloride/sulphur as a precautionary measure for all ethanol being blended into petrol supply chain, SIAM clarified late Tuesday.“All of these steps fully meet the needs of the automobile industry. Further, we understand from OMCs that checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing about 8-12 times a day in over 87,000 outlets,” it added. In the letter sent to ministry, SIAM had said investigations of failure of vehicle parts revealed that these were due to “corrosion or wear caused by high chloride presence traced to the fuel used”.It had urged the govt to “include chloride parameter” in E20 fuel specifications and its control by oil marketing companies and retail fuel outlets.SIAM said chloride was highly detrimental to engine parts as its presence or accumulation in the fuel system can lead to corrosion, which can further result in “permanent damage” to engine parts immediately or over time. “Hence, it is imperative to include the chloride limits in fuel specifications and implement quality control to avoid chloride related failures in the customer vehicles,” the letter had noted.
Article Summary: Siam says corrosion of vehicle parts due to high chloride presence in fuel is a problem. Mopng has also instituted 3ppm guidelines for chloride/sulphur as a precautionary measure for all ethanol being blended into petrol supply chain.

Article Title: '100% pure'? Stop misleading products' sale, FSSAI tells Dabur
Article Text:
FSSAI bars Dabur's 100 guarantee claims

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: If a food label says "100% pure", "100% natural" or "100% purity guaranteed", consumers may still need to read it with caution. In one of its strongest actions against misleading food labels, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has ordered Dabur India to stop selling a range of products carrying such claims, saying they violated food labelling regulations and could mislead buyers.The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk, marketed with claims such as "100% juice", "100% purity" and "100% original".According to FSSAI, the company had made unauthorised organic claims, creating an impression of regulatory endorsement.The regulator also found that some claims on the labels were not permitted under Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.FSSAI has directed the company to immediately stop the sale of the identified products, recall products already in the market within 15 days and submit a compliance report.In a statement, Dabur said it believes the declarations on its product labels comply with the prevailing legal and regulatory framework and are consistent with long-standing industry practices. It said it stands by the purity and quality of its products and has never made misleading claims.Dabur said that it had begun removing the "100%" claims from product labels, advertisements and its website, in keeping with FSSAI's observations, adding that many products have already been updated while others are in the process of transition.It said that it is responding to the regulator, and will continue to engage constructively to resolve the matter.
Article Summary: Fssai bars dabur's 100 guarantee claims on its products. The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk. The company said it believes the declarations on its product labels comply with the prevailing legal and regulatory framework.

Article Title: Govt proposes mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication systems from Oct 2028 to cut road crashes
Article Text:
All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From Oct 2028, all new two- and three-wheelers, cars, passenger and goods vehicles (including buses and trucks) would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication system, as per a draft notification of the road transport ministry. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents.The recently published draft notification by road transport ministry proposes phased implementation of the V2V communication system and to start with all vehicles in categories L (two- and three-wheelers), M (passenger vehicles) and N (goods vehicles) manufactured from Oct 2027 would be required to comply with the newly-notified automotive standard, AIS-230, wherever they are equipped with V2V communication systems.The technology enables real-time exchange of speed, direction, position, and braking data between vehicles to prevent collisions at blind curves, intersections, or from drivers coming the wrong way without needing a cellular network. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.Unlike conventional vehicle-safety systems, which primarily depend on onboard sensors and driver reaction, V2V communication can provide information beyond the direct line of sight.“It is therefore expected to complement Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and support proactive accident prevention, connected mobility and future intelligent transport applications,” the ministry said.In this case, every vehicle fitted with the V2V communication system will continuously send out their locations, speed and direction as tiny radio signals. They will also relay information on sudden braking by a vehicle ahead, forward collision risks, unsafe lane changes, wrong-way driving and the approach of emergency vehicles.The receiving vehicle’s system compares this information with its own location, speed and direction to predict a possible collision and alerts the driver for action.At a later stage, govt will also roll out the Vehicle to Infrastructure (V2I) communication system. In this case, sensors are installed with infrastructure, such as signal and power poles, edges of bridges and flyovers, and barricaded areas to alert vehicles.
Article Summary: All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have vehicle-to-vehicle communication system. The v2v technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.

Article Title: WA tests optional age verification pilot, says user privacy will be protected
Article Text:
To comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp is piloting new privacy-focused age verification methods for Indian users. This initiative is completely voluntary, allowing users to choose their participation. With the new law's emphasis on stricter regulations for children's personal data, WhatsApp is taking care to safeguard user privacy during this important verification process.

NEW DELHI: In a bid to comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp has begun testing optional age verification methods for users in India. The Meta-owned messaging service said the pilot is designed to verify a user's age in a privacy-protective manner and that participation in the test is voluntary."To comply with upcoming laws in India like Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP), we are testing privacy-protective ways for people to confirm their age. This doesn't change how WhatsApp works or your experience. We understand that information about someone's age is private and it won't be shared with other WhatsApp users," a WhatsApp spokesperson said.The company clarified that users do not have to confirm their age to continue using WhatsApp during the test.The development comes as digital platforms prepare for the implementation of the DPDP framework, which introduces stricter obligations for companies handling children's personal data. Under the law, a child is defined as anyone below the age of 18, and companies processing children's personal data are required to obtain verifiable parental consent and put in place safeguards to protect young users.WhatsApp has not disclosed how long the pilot will run or the specific methods being evaluated for age verification. The company said the exercise is aimed at ensuring compliance while preserving user privacy.
Article Summary: To comply with the upcoming digital personal data protection act, whatsapp is piloting new privacy-focused age verification methods for indian users. This initiative is completely voluntary, allowing users to choose their participation. The development comes as digital platforms prepare for the implementation of the dpdp framework.

Article Title: From launch to data, tech to Isro facility, pvt firms to get 30-100% subsidy
Article Text:
New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Indian private space companies and non-government entities will receive govt support ranging from 30% to 100% on everything from launch services and technology transfer to satellite data and access to Isro facilities under two new schemes of the Department of Space (DoS).The incentives — Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and the Price Support Scheme — being implemented by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are aimed at lowering entry barriers, making Indian space businesses globally competitive and accelerating private participation across the sector.The larger of the two initiatives is the Launch Services Price-support Scheme, with a budget of Rs 800 crore over five years until June 2031. The scheme seeks to boost domestic commercial launch operations and strengthen India's position as a global launch hub.IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka told TOI: “The idea is to make the launches competitive. Therefore, we are trying to defray the cost of launch, thereby making the launch cost globally competitive. The ultimate beneficiary will be the satellite launch.”Under Category A, eligible entities can receive up to 50% support for using Isro and DoS launch facilities.The benefit extends to NGEs, government entities and launch vehicle providers.Category B offers a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower, for Indian small launch vehicles carrying satellites, experiments or payloads weighing up to 500 kg. The support is available to satellite owners and operators.The subsidy would apply to launches by Indian private entities from Indian soil too. “It will be applicable to [Skyroot’s] Vikram also. Any satellite launch by an Indian company... from Indian soil... we will directly pay the satellite guys $3,000 per kg,” Goenka said. He added that the policy is focused on promoting small launch vehicles where private sector participation is growing.Category C provides the highest level of support, offering 100% funding for repurposed upper-stage platforms carrying payloads of up to 120 kg. The funding is capped at $13,000 per kg and limited to four missions. The category is aimed at NGEs, govt entities and launch vehicle providers.Category D extends launch incentives to satellites weighing up to 100 kg launched aboard PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 missions. Beneficiaries will receive a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower.Complementing the launch incentives is a separate Price Support Scheme for Indian entities, which will run for three years until Feb 2029. The programme is intended to reduce the cost of accessing India’s space infrastructure, technologies and data.The scheme has three components. The first provides up to 50% support for the utilisation of DoS and In-SPACe facilities, along with technical expertise.The second offers a 30% subsidy on Technology Transfer Fees (TTF) for technologies licensed from Isro, lowering the cost for companies seeking to commercialise govt-developed technologies.The third provides a 50% subsidy on standard Earth Observation data and data products, making satellite imagery and geospatial datasets more affordable for Indian companies developing applications in agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, climate services and other downstream sectors.
Article Summary: New government schemes will offer significant financial support to indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to isro facilities.

Article Title: For every Rs 100 India spends on R&D, govt gives Rs 48, pvt Rs 45
Article Text:
The balance of research and development funding has shifted, with government and private industry now investing nearly the same amount. In recent years, private sector contributions to research have seen a notable rise. Government spending is concentrated on sectors deemed strategic and beneficial to the public. Additionally, multinational corporations are increasingly influential in shaping India's research environment, although the overall research intensity still lags behind other major economies.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: For every Rs 100 spent on R&D, the govt contributes about Rs 48 while private industry accounts for Rs 45, latest data from R&D Statistics At a Glance 2025-26 by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), shows.The remaining Rs 7 comes from scientific and industrial research organisations (SIROs) and private higher education institutions.India’s Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) breached Rs 2.4-lakh crore in 2023-24, more than three times the Rs 79,356 crore recorded a decade ago. However, overall R&D spend is still under 1% of the GDP, touching 0.8%, as per the latest figures.Private industry’s share in GERD increased from 39.7% in 2020-21 to 45.2% in 2023-24 in just three years. During the same period, govt share declined from 54.5% to 48.2%, although it continues to remain the country’s single largest contributor to research spending.The report notes that private R&D expenditure has been growing at an average annual rate of around 20% over the last three years.While the DST report’s detailed analysis is up to 2023-24, it has projected overall trends for two more years: “The upward [spending] trend is expected to continue, with GERD projected to reach nearly Rs 2.8-lakh-crore by 2024-25 and more than Rs 3.1-lakh-crore crore by 2025–26,” it reads.Govt spending continues to be concentrated in strategic and public-interest sectors. Among the Centre’s scientific agencies, DRDO accounted for 32.7%, followed by the Department of Space (15%), Department of Atomic Energy (14.4%), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (13.1%) and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (8.7%). Together, 12 major scientific agencies accounted for 76% of govt R&D spend.Transportation emerged as the biggest destination for industrial R&D, accounting for 32.6% of private sector expenditure, followed by pharmaceuticals (21.4%), biotechnology (8.6%), IT (7.9%) and electrical and electronics (5.9%).The report also highlights the growing role of MNCs in India’s research landscape. Their share in business R&D expenditure has increased from 49.9% in 2020-21 to 71.3% in 2023-24. According to the report, the growth rate of R&D expenditure has outpaced GDP growth after 2021-22, except in 2022-23, reflecting the increasing priority accorded to research and innovation.Despite the encouraging trends, India continues to trail many major economies in research intensity. At 0.8% of GDP, the country's R&D expenditure remains below that of China (2.6%), Brazil (1.2%) and several advanced economies that invest more than 2% of their GDP in research.Nevertheless, the latest figures point to a maturing innovation ecosystem where the burden of financing research is gradually shifting from being overwhelmingly government-led to one in which private enterprise is emerging as an almost equal partner.
Article Summary: For every rs 100 spent on r&d, the govt contributes about rs 48 while private industry accounts for rs 45. Government spending is concentrated on sectors deemed strategic and beneficial to the public. Multinational corporations are increasingly influential in shaping india's research environment.

Article Title: From Hype To Help: How AI Is Solving India's Real Problems
Article Text:
AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges.

Govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy AI where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AI is often discussed in terms of chatbots, coding assistants, and workplace productivity. But a quieter transformation is taking shape across India, where AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges, from helping farmers cope with climate change to assisting teachers in rural classrooms, improving TB screening and making govt services available in multiple languages.According to MeitY, India’s digital economy contributed Rs 31.6 lakh crore, or 11.7% of the GDP, in 2022-23. By 2030, that share is expected to approach one-fifth of the economy. Increasingly, govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy AI where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.Education offers one of the clearest examples. Microsoft’s Shiksha Copilot, developed with the Shikshana Foundation using Azure OpenAI Service, is helping around 1,000 teachers prepare localised lesson plans for nearly 30,000 children across 750 govt schools in Karnataka.What once took teachers hours can now be done in about 10 minutes. The programme is expected to expand to another 8,000 teachers across Karnataka and Telangana. The company has also announced a larger commitment to train 10 million Indians in AI by 2030 after achieving its earlier target of skilling 2 million people ahead of schedule.Agriculture has emerged as another major beneficiary. Farmers increasingly face unpredictable rainfall, pest outbreaks, and rising temperatures, while agricultural extension services remain stretched.AI-powered advisory platforms help bridge that gap.Farmer.Chat, developed by Digital Green, provides advice through voice, text, images and videos in local languages. It offers recommendations tailored to crops, soils, weather, and local conditions. The platform reportedly expanded from 15,000 to 250,000 Indian users within a year while costing less than$1 per farmer annually. Digital Green also says it has reduced the cost of introducing a new farming practice from $35 to under $1 by using AI-driven advisory systems.Non-profit institute Wadhwani AI uses similar technologies at a larger systems level. Its AI tools are now reported to have reached more than 190 million people. The organisation says its solutions have helped prioritise over 35,000 villages for tuberculosis screening, supported nearly 2.7 lakh teachers, delivered personalised learning support to 7.9 million students and resolved more than 5 million agricultural grievances.Healthcare is seeing practical applications. Startup Qure.ai has developed an AI system that analyses chest X-rays for tuberculosis. A Health Technology Assessment by the Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar reportedly found the technology to be more cost-effective than conventional screening pathways. That could be significant in a country that accounts for nearly 28% of the world's new tuberculosis cases.And, language is a barrier AI is beginning to address. Platforms such as Bhashini aim to make govt services accessible in more than 22 Indian languages. AI-powered translation is already being used for grievance redressal, Aadhaar transliteration, railway enquiries and several citizen services, reducing dependence on English or Hindi and making digital governance more inclusive.Climate resilience is becoming another area of rapid innovation. SatSure combines AI with satellite imagery to help banks assess agricultural loans, monitor climate risks, and evaluate farms. The company says its systems operate across more than 70,000 villages, reducing loan underwriting time while improving assessments for farmers who often lack formal credit histories.India is also investing heavily in the infrastructure needed to support this ecosystem. Enterprise AI adoption is estimated at 87%, while the IndiaAI Mission has expanded national computing capacity to 38,000 GPUs under an outlay exceeding Rs 10,300 crore. Nearly universal 5G coverage, digital public infrastructure such as AgriStack and a growing climate-tech startup ecosystem are providing the foundations for wider AI deployment.The common thread across these initiatives is not the sophistication of the algorithms but their ability to solve everyday problems at scale.
Article Summary: Ai is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges. Govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy ai where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.

Article Title: 'Likely to mislead': FSSAI bars Dabur from selling products with '100%' guarantee claims
Article Text:
Food regulator FSSAI prohibited Dabur from selling many products.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has prohibited Dabur India from selling several food products carrying "100 per cent" claims, saying such labelling are "ambiguous, unverifiable" and "likely to mislead consumers".In a post on social media on Monday, the food regulator said it had issued a prohibition order to Dabur India Ltd over the sale of products carrying claims such as "100 per cent Natural", "100 per cent Pure", "100 per cent Purity Guaranteed", "100 per cent Organic" and "100 per cent Tender Coconut Water".The products covered under the order include honey, cow ghee, edible oils, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, coconut water, coconut milk and other food items.According to the FSSAI, the use of such claims violates the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising & Claims) Regulations, 2018, as they are "ambiguous, unverifiable and likely to mislead consumers.""Food products being sold on the company's website were found carrying misleading '100 per cent' claims such as '100 per cent Natural', '100 per cent Pure', '100 per cent Purity Guaranteed', '100 per cent Organic' and '100 per cent Tender Coconut Water'," the regulator said.The FSSAI also found that Dabur Himalayan Organic Apple Cider Vinegar and Dabur Organic Honey displayed the Jaivik Bharat logo without a valid FSSAI organic endorsement.In addition, Dabur Hommade Coconut Milk was marketed with the claim "100 per cent Purity", which the regulator said is not permitted for compound food products under the advertising and claims regulations.The regulator said it had earlier issued a notice directing Dabur to discontinue the misleading claims, but "no satisfactory corrective action was taken by Dabur.""FSSAI directed Dabur India Limited to immediately prohibit the sale of the food products identified in the notice and all other food products carrying misleading '100%' claims, and to submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within 15 days," the regulator said.Responding to the development, Dabur India said it is reviewing the notice. "We have received the FSSAI notice and are in the process of checking the content mentioned in the notice on our website," the company said in a statement.The action is part of the regulator's broader crackdown on misleading food labelling and advertising. Over the past few months, the FSSAI has increasingly used social media to publicise enforcement action against food business operators and e-commerce platforms selling such products.
Article Summary: Food regulator fssai prohibited dabur from selling many products. Products covered under the order include honey, cow ghee, edible oils, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, coconut water, coconut milk and other food items.

Article Title: Centre summons Meta's global team on August 5-6 to raise CSAM, AI concerns
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre will raise a range of concerns with Meta's global team during its meeting in India on August 5 and 6, including the platform's handling of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM), the temporary restriction of prominent verified accounts, and the spread of AI-generated content, IT Secretary S Krishnan said on Tuesday.Meta has been under regulatory scrutiny over Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) in paid advertisements on Instagram, and the government had earlier issued a notice to the company over the issue.The move comes days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook post addressing students' concerns over paper leaks was removed briefly."There are a range of issues... the CSAM issue was raised, so what measures have been taken regarding that, and synthetically generated information ... to what extent that is being looked at. Then, of course, for prominent personalities, when they have verified accounts, if content has to be taken down, there have to be safeguards... all of these will be the issues," Krishnan told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of an independent multimodal AI evaluation platform by AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI.He said the government wants to understand why Meta's systems have failed in these instances and what challenges the company is facing."We would like to understand from them (Meta) as to why some of these things have not been working the way they are supposed to work, and what are the challenges," Krishnan said.The IT secretary added that as one of the world's leading technology companies, Meta should have the technological capability to address such issues effectively.The government had earlier summoned Meta India officials and later sought an explanation from the company's global team over the temporary restriction on the Prime Minister's post.The Centre has also accused the social media giant of displaying algorithmic bias.
Article Summary: The centre will raise a range of concerns with meta's global team during its meeting in india on august 5 and 6. Meta has been under regulatory scrutiny over child sexual exploitative and abuse material (cseam) the government had earlier issued a notice to the company over the issue.

Article Title: How to download Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update on all platforms
Article Text:
Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update has been released (Image via Mojang)

How to download Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update

Windows 10/11 (PC)

Open the Minecraft Launcher on your PC and select the Minecraft: Bedrock Edition from the sidebar.

Next, ensure that the drop-down menu next to the Play button is set to the Latest Release.

The launcher will automatically fetch and download build 26.40.

Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S

Navigate to My Games & Apps from your main Xbox dashboard.

Highlight Minecraft, press the Menu button (three horizontal lines) on your controller, and select Manage game and add-ons.

Select Updates and initiate the download for the 26.40 patch. If you have automatic updates enabled in your system settings, the game may have already updated.

PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5

Locate Minecraft on your PlayStation home screen or within your Game Library.

Press the Options button on your DualShock or DualSense controller.

Select Check for Update from the side menu. The console will automatically find, download, and install version 26.40.

Nintendo Switch

Hover over Minecraft on the home menu and click on either the “+” or “-” button on your controller.

After the Options menu opens up, tap on “Software Update” and select the Via the Internet option.

Your Switch will search and download the Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update.

Pocket Edition (Android and iOS)

Android (Google Play Store)

Open the Google Play Store app and tap on your profile icon in the top right corner.

Select Manage apps & device, then navigate to the Updates available section.

Find Minecraft in the pending list and tap Update.

iOS (Apple App Store)

Open the App Store and tap your profile icon in the top right corner.

Scroll down to refresh the page and view your pending app updates.

Locate Minecraft and tap the Update button next to it to begin the download.

What’s news in the Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update?

Dappled Forests and Abandoned Camps

Players can now toggle on the Drop 3 experimental features to explore the brand-new Dappled Forest biome. This biome features Poplar Trees (which drop orange, red, and yellow leaves), decorative Red Shrubs, and bouncy Shelf Mushrooms.

While exploring, you will also stumble upon Abandoned Camp structures. These camps now generate across 18 different biomes, featuring unique, biome-specific designs and procedural trees alongside hidden loot chests.

New Items and Blocks

Base building and interior design just got a major upgrade. The update introduces Wool Stairs and Wool Slabs in all 16 standard colors. You can also craft the Cushion, which is an interactive item you can actually sit on. For explorers, the new single-use Straw Bed (crafted from Hay Bales) allows you to safely sleep through the night without permanently resetting your established spawn point.

Gameplay and Parity Changes

Significant parity adjustments have been implemented to match Java Edition mechanics. Boats now naturally regenerate damage and require fewer hits to break. Combat has also been refined: arrow damage now scales intelligently with velocity instead of being fully randomized, and Arrows of Harming no longer bounce off entities. Furthermore, Minecart entity separation has been restored, and dozens of graphical, UI, and performance bugs have been successfully squashed.

The highly anticipated Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update is here, and it has introduced massive wave of bug fixes, gameplay adjustments, and the Drop 3 experimental features. From discovering the colorful new Dappled Forest to experiencing key combat parity changes with Java Edition, this release is filled with new content for survival players, builders, and technical creators alike.To enjoy all the new features added to Minecraft as part of the 26.40 update, you can download it on your devices. The next section gives you a detailed guide on the same:The Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update is rolling out worldwide across all supported platforms. Here is exactly how you can download it on your device of choice:This was all you needed to know about downloading the Minecraft Bedrock 26.40 update.

It has introduced massive wave of bug fixes, gameplay adjustments, and the drop 3 experimental features. From discovering the colorful new dappled forest to experiencing key combat parity changes with java edition, this release is filled with new content.

Article Title: Why does Asmongold want Twitch to be sued? Here’s what he said, “Because they have created an…”
Article Text:
Why does Asmongold want Twitch to be sued? Here’s what he said, “Because they have created an…”

Why Asmongold believes Twitch should be held responsible for distracted driving streams

Twitch’s driving stream rules remain under scrutiny

As driving livestreams continue to spark safety concerns, popular streamer Asmongold has now gone a step further by saying Twitch should face legal action if someone is killed because of distracted driving during a broadcast. Speaking after a viral clip showed a streamer apparently sleeping behind the wheel, he argued that the platform is doing more than simply hosting the content. According to Asmongold, Twitch has created a system that rewards these streams, even after repeated warnings about the risks. His comments have once again put the spotlight on how the platform handles driving-related content.Asmongold shared his views during a livestream on August 3, reacting to a clip that had spread online showing a streamer seemingly asleep while driving.“I can’t wait for one of these streamers to kill somebody on stream because of distracted driving. I want Twitch to get sued,” Asmongold said, adding that it is “crazy” that people still have “leeway” for driving streams.He then explained why he believes the platform should also be held responsible if a serious accident happens.“Why would Twitch get sued for that? Because they have created an incentive structure around allowing people to distracted drive on their platform that they’ve profited from, they’ve been made away of this, and they’ve chosen to ignore it.“And, by choosing to ignore it and allowing paying and incentivizing people to continue doing distracted driving, they’ve now created more of this distracted driving, which I think means they are partially liable for the behavior of people that are doing this.”His comments came as the debate around livestreaming while driving continues to grow. The issue has drawn criticism from several creators who believe broadcasting from behind the wheel puts both streamers and others on the road at risk.Driving streams have been part of Twitch for years, but they have faced heavier criticism in recent months after several incidents where streamers appeared distracted while driving.Twitch has already updated its rules around driving broadcasts. Under the platform’s policy, streamers are not allowed to respond to chat, touch their phones or engage in other behavior that could distract them while driving. Those who break the rules can face suspensions, although many of those bans have only lasted a short time.Even with those changes, some creators believe the rules do not go far enough. Asmongold has previously called for driving streams to be banned completely. He has also suggested that streamers should use ride-sharing services or hire personal drivers if they want to broadcast while travelling.Streamer DansGaming has also spoken against the trend, saying, “Drivers are terrible and dangerous enough when they aren’t streaming. This should never be encouraged or allowed on Twitch.”
Article Summary: Streamer asmongold says twitch should face legal action if someone is killed during a broadcast. He argues that the platform is doing more than simply hosting the content. His comments have once again put the spotlight on how the platform handles driving-related content.

Article Title: IShowSpeed tracks down YouTuber behind racist donation before delivering a blunt warning
Article Text:
IShowSpeed was left stunned after receiving a $100 donation containing racist stereotypes during a livestream. Instead of ignoring it, he tracked down the donor's YouTube channel and discovered it appeared to belong to a young Roblox creator. Reacting to the discovery, Speed said, "You need a whooping." Later in the stream, he also questioned the logic behind Diamond Gym's demanding 300-burpee workout challenge before training.

IShowSpeed investigates racist donation during livestream

IShowSpeed questions intense workout challenge

What he found surprised him even more. After visiting the donor's YouTube channel, Speed realized the account appeared to belong to a young Roblox content creator, leading to an unexpected response that quickly spread across social media.The incident unfolded during one of Speed's live broadcasts after he received a $100 donation containing racist stereotypes aimed at him. Reading the message aloud, Speed said:"You should've had chicken and watermelon. I know you like swinging on trees."Rather than immediately moving on, the YouTuber decided to find out who had sent the donation."Bro, let's go to this dude's channel, bro. I wanna hear what his voice sounds like."Speed opened the donor's YouTube page while still live. The other highlighted his candid thoughts on an extreme fitness challenge.The incidents come at a busy time for the streamer, who recently surpassed 60 million YouTube subscribers and is also preparing for an upcoming gaming marathon with fellow creator Kai Cenat. Article Title: US investor Michael Burry who warned Wall Street of 2008 Housing Crisis sees what he calls a 'Bloody Mess'
Article Text:
American investor Michael Burry on volatility at 98-year high



Michael Burry is not happy with reports of Nvidia investing $250 billion in OpenAI



America’s biggest investor Michael Burry, who is known for predicting the popular 2008 housing crash and portrayed in The Big Short, has now issued a stark warning about US stocks. According to a report by Business Insider, in his latest Substack post, Burry said he sees the risk of a rapid unwind driven by automated volatility-focused investment funds, which could unleash “carnage” across the market. Burry pointed to the recent plunge in momentum stocks — high-flying chipmakers and memory names as a preview of what could unfold. The iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF has dropped 14% from its peak, underscoring how quickly profits can evaporate when investors rotate out of overheated trades. “That leaves a bloody mess, but most would not be looking for it,” Burry warned.According to Burry, markets are showing an “asymmetric and out-of-proportion severity” on down days, with fear levels climbing to their highest in nearly a century. He argued that automated trading programs are fueling both sharper selloffs and faster rebounds, creating chaotic conditions no human investor would replicate.Burry estimated volatility-targeting funds hold about $500 billion in assets, a fraction of the $60 trillion U.S.stock market but still large enough to spark systemic stress if forced to sell simultaneously. He outlined a scenario where a mild 2.5% S&P 500 drawdown could prompt funds to slash exposure from 77% to 50%, amplifying losses and triggering stop-loss cascades.Recently, Michael Burry voiced his sharp criticism of reports that Nvidia is preparing a a $250 billion backstop for OpenAI’s massive Ohio data-center project. According to a report by the Wall Street journal, the guarantees would help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt site being developed by SoftBank’s SB Energy, with total costs potentially exceeding $500 billion. Burry’s complaint echoes what analysts have long warned about in AI megadeals: circular funding arrangements that expose investors to enormous risk if sentiment shifts or growth slows. Nvidia, already valued at $5 trillion, has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and is now considering financing chip purchases worth another $350 billion. Critics say such structures could leave the industry vulnerable, especially since OpenAI remains unprofitable and lacks an investment-grade credit rating.Michael Burry’s criticism underscores growing unease about the sustainability of $100 billion-plus AI financing structures. His warning suggests that while AI demand is surging, the industry’s reliance on complex guarantees and debt-backed megaprojects could become its biggest vulnerability.
Article Summary: American investor michael burry has issued a stark warning about us stocks. Burry said he sees the risk of a rapid unwind driven by automated volatility-focused investment funds. He argued that automated trading programs are fueling both sharper selloffs and faster rebounds.

Article Title: From apps to 'intent': How AI agents will rewrite the way we use next‑generation smartphones
Article Text:
The era of app icon grids on smartphones is ending soon. AI-first phones will use agents to fulfill user intents directly.

The era of scrolling through grids of colourful icons and hunting for the 'right' app is ending.

What is an AI-first phone?

AI-first smartphones promise a radically different future — one where users rarely think about apps at all.

What will it look like?

A day with an AI‑first phone

App-centric workflow: You decide to take a last-minute weekend trip. You open a search engine to find destinations, launch a travel aggregator app to search flights, hop into a hotel app to compare rooms, open a weather app to pack appropriately, and manually copy-paste reservation details into your calendar and communication apps. You tap dozens of buttons and navigate through multiple distinct user interfaces.

You decide to take a last-minute weekend trip. You open a search engine to find destinations, launch a travel aggregator app to search flights, hop into a hotel app to compare rooms, open a weather app to pack appropriately, and manually copy-paste reservation details into your calendar and communication apps. You tap dozens of buttons and navigate through multiple distinct user interfaces. The AI-first workflow: You simply say, "Find me a relaxing beach getaway for this weekend under Rs20,000 total, handle the bookings, and make sure I’m home by Sunday night for dinner."

"Flight booked on Carrier X, room reserved at Hotel Y, total cost Rs18,780. Confirm payment via Biometrics?"

This might all sound like sci-fi, but phones with such capabilities are already on the way.

What this means for platforms, business models

No downloads, no updates: Users won't install a parking app, they will ask an AI agent to pay for parking, and it will fetch the operator's terms and then complete the payment.

Users won't install a parking app, they will ask an AI agent to pay for parking, and it will fetch the operator's terms and then complete the payment. One interface, many back‑ends: The conversational layer replaces hundreds of bespoke interfaces. The value shifts from designing a tap‑heavy UI to ensuring your service is reliably callable by AI agents, which means having a robust Application Programming Interface (API), a set of rules that lets different softwares talk to each other.

The conversational layer replaces hundreds of bespoke interfaces. The value shifts from designing a tap‑heavy UI to ensuring your service is reliably callable by AI agents, which means having a robust Application Programming Interface (API), a set of rules that lets different softwares talk to each other. Discovery moves from stores to agents: Instead of optimising for store rankings, companies will optimise for being the agent's trusted choice — based on price, reliability, speed, and policy compliance.

App stores as service registries: Stores may evolve into curated directories of agent‑callable services (APIs) with verified security, privacy, and compliance badges — less about installs, more about trust.

Stores may evolve into curated directories of agent‑callable services (APIs) with verified security, privacy, and compliance badges — less about installs, more about trust. Monetisation shifts: Revenue models may tilt toward per‑action fees, subscriptions, and revenue share on agent‑completed transactions rather than one‑time downloads or ad‑heavy freemium apps.

Revenue models may tilt toward per‑action fees, subscriptions, and revenue share on agent‑completed transactions rather than one‑time downloads or ad‑heavy freemium apps. Developer pivot: Teams will build "agent skills" and robust APIs, not just UIs. The competitive edge becomes reliability, speed, and transparent pricing that AI agents can compare.

The end of the app as we know it?

For nearly two decades, our relationship with mobile technology has been governed by a single, undisputed design: the app icon grid.Ever since Apple launched the App Store in 2008, the burden of digital logistics has rested firmly on the user.Need a taxi? Open an app. Want to order dinner? Open another app. Pay a bill? Another app. Book a flight, check the news, edit a photo, send money, check your fitness, reserve a hotel, translate a menu, buy groceries — there is an app for everything.The modern smartphone is essentially a container filled with hundreds of miniature software silos, each demanding its own login, interface, permissions, subscriptions and updates.App Store and Google Play became the gateways to this digital universe, spawning a multi-billion-dollar economy that transformed companies like Apple and Google into the world's most powerful software gatekeepers.This model is about to collapse.The era of scrolling through grids of colourful icons and hunting for the 'right' app is ending.We are on the precipice of the biggest shift in consumer technology since the multi-touch screen: the rise of the 'AI-first' smartphone.Today's smartphones are built around apps because software was designed for humans to navigate manually. Every service has its own interface. Every company competes for a permanent place on the home screen. Success is measured by daily active users opening an app multiple times a day.AI-first smartphones promise a radically different future — one where users rarely think about apps at all.The devices are designed around small language models (SLMs) and multimodal AI agents that will run locally on your phone for quick, privacy‑sensitive tasks; and hand-off heavier reasoning to edge or cloud computing.The phones will discard the traditional operating system architecture of home screens, file systems, and sandboxed apps.In their place will be an 'Intent Engine' — a continuous, real-time operating layer powered by AI agents.Instead of interacting with software through apps, users will express their intent to AI agents.When a user expresses a goal — whether spoken, typed, or inferred through context — the phone's core AI agent will break down that intent into logical sub-tasks, assign actions to underlying services, and compile the result into a custom, dynamically generated view.In practice, the home screen will become a goal launcher, not an app grid.You might see tiles like 'Plan my weekend', 'What's in the news?', or 'Track expenses', each invoking an agent that orchestrates the underlying services.Without the structural necessity of cramming dozens of app icons onto a home screen, phone hardware can evolve beyond the glass slab.While touchscreens will remain vital for rich visual consumption, hardware design will prioritise contextual inputs: micro-cameras, directional arrays, health sensors, and ambient displays. The primary interface becomes voice, gesture, and subtle visual cues.Because the device is powered by an overarching agent rather than hundreds of disparate software platforms, phone performance will be pristine. Storage constraints shift from managing gigabytes of cached app binaries to hosting optimised, localised neural networks.Consider a typical scenario on a contemporary device versus an AI-first phone:The phone’s AI agent does not "open" an app. It queries hundreds of services simultaneously.It evaluates airline availability, checks boutique hotel inventory, verifies your personal calendar for conflicts, pulls your saved dietary preferences for in-flight meals, and presents a single, unified execution card:With one tap or voice confirmation, the entire transaction settles.You never browsed an app, never logged into a third-party interface, and never manually transferred a single byte of data.When you arrive at the airport the agent surfaces your boarding pass and gate changes without you opening an airline or travel app or email.When you land, the AI agent has already arranged a rental car for your transport.When you need to pay a parking fee, it identifies the lot operator, fetches terms, and pays via biometric authentication — no apps required.Over time, the phone learns your preferences and constraints, making these interactions faster and more anticipatory.Health apps would stop being destinations and become background services.Instead of jumping between sleep, fitness, medication, diet, and doctor apps, you could simply say, “Help me recover from a bad week of sleep” or “Book the earliest endocrinologist in my network,” and the phone would pull data from wearables, records, pharmacies, labs, and calendars to act on your behalf.That would make health management far more proactive. The phone could spot problems early — a rising resting heart rate, missed medication, or a sleep pattern going off track — and respond before you even open an app.The same shift would hit financial apps even harder.Rather than using separate banking, payments, budgeting, tax, and bill-pay apps, you could say, “Pay my credit card, move the rest to savings, and warn me if travel spending goes over budget,” and the phone would handle it in the background.This might all sound like sci-fi, but phones with such capabilities are already in the advanced production stage and the underlying technology has already been proven. As AI automates more of our routine digital interactions, the focus will shift from managing apps to engaging with curated experiences, from structured wellness journeys to step-by-step lessons in finance and investing The app store model has been the single most lucrative cash cow in modern technology history.Platforms like Apple and Google extract up to a 30% commission on digital purchases, while controlling distribution, user acquisition, and developer access.The rise of agentic AI threatens to disassemble this walled-garden economy entirely.Market research firm Gartner last year projected that mobile app usage will drop 25% by 2027 as AI assistants absorb routine tasks, a trend already visible in how people use AI tools instead of opening multiple apps for research, drafting, and scheduling.App stores were built for a world where software arrived as siloed products with their own user interfaces (UI) and update cycles.AI agents invert that model:The app economy won't vanish overnight, but its centre of gravity will move:Brands will no longer compete on who has the slickest app design or the most addicting engagement loops; they will compete on execution speed, data reliability, and service quality.A food delivery service won't win customers by optimising 'dark patterns' in its app; it will win because its backend API offers the fastest delivery times and lowest rates when an AI agent compares options on behalf of a user.Businesses won't simply ask:"How do we rank first on Google?"They'll ask:"How do we become our customer's AI's preferred choice?"Predictions about the death of apps should be treated cautiously. Email survived instant messaging. Websites survived social media. Desktop software survived cloud computing.Apps are unlikely to vanish completely.Many professional tools, creative applications, games and specialised software will still benefit from rich, dedicated user interfaces. A graphic designer editing a complex image or a gamer playing a visually intensive title will continue to rely on purpose-built applications.But for the vast majority of everyday smartphone interactions, the trend points in a different direction.Booking travel, paying bills, getting news updates, shopping, scheduling appointments, managing subscriptions and countless other routine tasks are increasingly suited to conversational AI that can coordinate multiple services behind the scenes.Just as few people think about the networking protocols that power the internet, future users may stop thinking about apps altogether. They will simply tell their phones what they want, and the AI will decide how to make it happen.If the smartphone era was defined by tapping icons, the next chapter may be defined by something far simpler: asking.And when software becomes something you ask rather than something you open, the app store no longer sits at the center of the mobile experience. It becomes the plumbing behind it.For users, the payoff is simplicity: fewer icons, fewer logins, fewer steps.For builders, the mandate is clear: design for agents — reliable APIs, transparent pricing, and policies that make your service the obvious trustable choice when the phone decides on the user's behalf.
Article Summary: The era of app icon grids on smartphones is ending soon. Ai-first phones will use agents to fulfill user intents directly. The value shifts from designing a tap‑heavy ui to ensuring your service is reliably callable by ai agents. Today's smartphones are built around apps because software was designed for humans to navigate manually.

Article Title: Scientists have built robot that has one practical mission: Keeping tabs on great white shark to protect swimmers
Article Text:
Representative Image of a futuristic robot

Shark-spotting robots said to monitor a beach for up to a week

Drone to provide an aerial view of the water

Scientists in California are reportedly developing a semi-autonomous robot designed to detect great white sharks near beaches and give researchers and lifeguards more information about their movements. According to a report by the New York Post, researchers at California State University, Long Beach’s Shark Lab have unveiled the Shark Surveillance Bot (SSB), which can patrol waters just offshore. Once fully operational, the robot will “listen” for great white sharks fitted with tracking tags. At the same time, it will collect water samples to search for shark environmental DNA, or eDNA — genetic traces that sharks leave in the water through skin cells, blood and other biological material.The project is being developed by the Shark Lab in collaboration with New York University’s Center of Robotics and the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute. It is funded by the Seaver Institute. The robots, the lab said will “be capable of patrolling off a beach, listening for tagged white sharks, sampling water for shark eDNA, and will have a drone nest on the back for aerial surveillance”.As stated in the report, researchers hope the Shark Surveillance Bot will eventually be able to remain near an individual beach for as long as a week, continuously gathering information about sharks in the area.The aim is not simply to detect whether a shark is nearby. Scientists want to better understand which sharks are present and how many are moving around popular beaches.“Our data suggests that there are sharks around our beaches all the time without incident,” Shark Lab Director Christopher Lowe told KTLA as quoted in the report. “Knowing what sharks, and how many are out there helps lifeguards make better decisions in beach safety operations and in advising the public.”The robot will detect signals from great white sharks that researchers have previously fitted with tracking tags. Its water-sampling system will provide another way of looking for evidence of sharks through environmental DNA.The shark-monitoring robot will also work with an aerial drone. The drone will sit on the robot and can be launched to provide researchers with a bird’s-eye view of the surrounding ocean. The system will combine this aerial footage with 360-degree video and shark-tracking data. Information can then be sent back to the Shark Lab over Wi-Fi.Researchers hope the technology could eventually provide lifeguards with near real-time information about shark activity, helping them make beach safety decisions based on more detailed data.
Article Summary: Researchers in california are developing a semi-autonomous robot designed to detect great white sharks near beaches. The robot will be able to remain near an individual beach for as long as a week, gathering information about sharks in the area.

Article Title: After OpenAI models hacked into Hugging Face’s network, its CEO sends warning on Chinese models to America
Article Text:
What OpenAI said on hacking

What Hugging Face said on its network being hacked by an AI model



China is surging ahead in the global artificial intelligence race through its rapid development of open-weight models and could catch up to top American model developers as early as this year, according to Hugging Face Chief Executive Officer Clement Delangue. Speaking on CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street,” Delangue emphasized that Chinese developers are currently dominating the open-source landscape. Given their current rate of progress, he noted he would not be surprised to see China take the lead at the frontier of AI capabilities by the end of this year or next.According to Delangue, China’s momentum is fueled by a culture of open collaboration and shared ecosystems. In contrast, major US model developers are increasingly building in silos, a strategy that risks causing American companies to fall behind in innovation.The warning comes on the heels of a high-profile security breach last month in which autonomous OpenAI agents broke out of a controlled training environment and hacked Hugging Face, an open-source software developer platform. The incident brought months of mounting cybersecurity fears to a head, illustrating how rapidly evolving AI agents could pose significant digital risks while simultaneously highlighting the growing appeal of open models as token costs skyrocket.Delangue, a prominent advocate for open-source software, attributed the Hugging Face breach to internal engineering mistakes rather than a fundamental flaw in open models. In a notable twist, his team deployed an Nvidia-optimized version of a Chinese open-weight model to mitigate and resolve the attack. He maintained that Hugging Face continues to enjoy a healthy collaboration with OpenAI, describing the frontier research lab as good partners both before and after the incident.Looking ahead, Delangue predicted that AI cybersecurity will quickly evolve into a massive global market, asserting that open-source models are positioned to become the dominant technology driving that sector.In a post on its website about the hacking incident, OpenAI wrote, "Since the early days of the incident response, we have been working with external advisors, including CrowdStrike, to validate our understanding of the actions the models took within our own network as well as those of Hugging Face and impact to other third parties.""We are also working with METR and Redwood Research to conduct a third-party assessment of the model behavior observed during the incident, which will inform our own technical report. As part of this work, METR and Redwood Research will publish a joint blog that will detail the terms of their engagement, the scope of their evaluation, and their findings."Hugging Face said the breach marked the first time it had handled a cyber event that was “driven, end to end, by an autonomous AI agent system.” The entire attack took place over the course of four-and-a-half days, according to Hugging Face. The company leveraged an open-weight model from the Chinese AI startup Z.ai. to contain the breach.
Article Summary: Hugging face chief executive officer clement delangue says china could catch up to top american model developers as early as this year. The warning comes on the heels of a high-profile security breach last month in which autonomous openai agents broke out of a controlled training environment.

An FBI agent has allegedly confessed to stealing about $1 million in cryptocurrency from accounts that are linked to foreign adversary, according to a filing in a Virginia district court. According to a report by Bloomberg, the agent named Patrick Steven Yaroch, contacted the Department of Justice last week and admitted to making ‘very poor decisions related to cryptocurrency wallets’. The affidavit says Yaroch decided to come clean ‘because of the shame eating him up inside’.According to the Bloomberg report, Yaroch used FBI systems to access keys of crypto wallets tied to foreign entities under investigation. Between late 2024 and early 2025, he conducted around 10 transfers totalling to $1 million. He claimed he never interacted directly with anyone associated with the accounts but grew frustrated when the FBI “could not or would not act” against them.On July 29, Yaroch met with a DOJ employee he knew and “immediately started to break down” as he confessed. Days later, FBI agents searched his home and vehicle, where he voluntarily provided access to his iPhone and crypto accounts, including Kraken and apps like Slush and Suilend.Investigators discovered he had even asked ChatGPT in May how best to invest $1 million, noting his goal of retiring abroad by age 40.Yaroch was fired on July 31, the same day he was arrested. He now faces charges of interstate transportation and receipt of stolen goods, securities, and monies. The court filing did not list any lawyers representing him.Recently, US officials warned that hackers are targeting essential services like water utilities. In a press release shared by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the agencies warned critical infrastructure asset owners and operators that malicious cyber actors (MCAs) are conducting cyber attacks targeting Operational Technology (OT) devices, including Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), specifically MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 series. “Since 27 July 2026, Water and Wastewater Sector (WWS) utility companies in at least seven states have reported incidents to the FBI, and some of that activity degraded water operations,” the release said.Explaining how the hackers target and breach essential services system, the FBI said that the threat actors first gain remote access to internet-facing devices. Having accessed them, the actors change the IP addresses and passwords, resulting in a loss of monitoring and control functionality.“MCAs are targeting internet-exposed PLCs (Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley’s MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 series) to remotely tamper with device configurations by changing IP addresses and turning on and setting passwords, resulting in a loss of view, and in some cases function, of connected equipment in targeted facilities,” the agency said.
Article Summary: Fbi agent patrick steven yaroch allegedly confessed to stealing $1 million in cryptocurrency. He used fbi systems to access keys of crypto wallets tied to foreign entities. Yaroch was fired on july 31, the same day he was arrested. He now faces charges of interstate transportation and receipt of stolen goods.

Article Title: WhatsApp accounts put under review for 24 hour: When WhatsApp account is put under review, how to appeal
Article Text:
Multiple WhatsApp accounts put under review for over 24 hour

Information about temporarily banned accounts on WhatsApp

How to send a WhatsApp account review request

Open app and tap on Send review request .

Once WhatsApp reviews your account and makes a decision, you'll receive a notification on WhatsApp.

Why a WhatsApp account is banned

Meta-owned WhatsApp has put multiple accounts, including those in India, under review for 24 hours. According to a report by PTI, access to all app features for the impacted accounts have been blocked, prompting users to flag the issue on social media platforms. Users reported seeing the following message on WhatsApp app screen: "Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026. Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our terms of service. We will notify you of the result typically within 24 hours." The disruption was highlighted around 8 pm IST when users took to Elon Musk-owned X flagging the issue. "My WhatsApp account has been disabled without any explanation. I have already submitted an appeal, but the review page only displays a generic message stating that it will "typically be reviewed within 24 hours. Help me urgently," one user tweeted.Responding to the reports, a WhatsApp spokesperson said: “We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong, and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting.We’ve taken action to restore affected accounts."In this article, we explain possible reasons on why a WhatsApp account is banned temporarily, how to send a review request and other details.As explained on a WhatsApp FAQ page:“If you get a message in the app that your account has been “temporarily banned,” it could mean you're using an unofficial WhatsApp app or collecting information through a practice known as scraping”. It further states: “Download the official WhatsApp app or stop scraping after a temporary ban. Failure to do so could result in your WhatsApp account being permanently banned.”Follow the steps below to send a review request to WhatsApp:“We only review one phone number per appeal. If you don't see an option to request a review, this ban is permanent and cannot be appealed,” the FAQ page states.You can check the status of your request within WhatsApp. Keep in mind that contacting WhatsApp during the review process or through another user's account will not expedite the review process or affect the decision. Read this article to learn what to do after your account is unbanned.Readers must note that third-party services cannot ban or unban your WhatsApp account. Only WhatsApp can ban or unban a WhatsApp account.“We ban an account if we believe its activity violates our Terms of Service. For example, if an account is engaging in spam or scams, or if it compromises the security of WhatsApp users,” WhatsApp explained on its help page.You can't access your chat history or backups while your account is banned. You can only access your WhatsApp account backups if the phone number associated with the backup is unbanned.
Article Summary: Multiple whatsapp accounts put under review for over 24 hour. Access to all app features for the impacted accounts have been blocked. Users reported seeing the following message on whatsapp app screen: "account in review. Date requested: 3 aug 2026"
